blocks.text: India: Union Budget Fiscal Framework, FY2025-26
Budget Estimates (BE), US$ unless stated. Union Budget 2025-26 (BE), PRS India, indiabudget.gov.in, as compiled in the source workbook.

All rupee figures are converted to US dollars (billions and millions) at ₹95.88 per US$ (Yahoo Finance, 2026-09-19). One current rate is applied to every year, so US$ trends across years ignore how the rupee moved over time (it is weaker now than in FY21), which understates US$ growth against a historical-rate conversion. Percent-of-GDP and other ratios are unaffected.
The consolidation path
Where each rupee of spending goes (FY26 BE)
Key insights
Interest is the single biggest item: $133.1 bn, 25.2% of all spending and 37.3% of revenue receipts.
Fiscal deficit of 4.4% of GDP is down from 9.3% in FY20-21 (workbook series). Primary deficit is 0.8%, so most of the remaining gap is interest.
Capital expenditure is $116.9 bn (3.1% of GDP) against $106.2 bn in FY24-25 RE: +10.1%.
Food and fertiliser are 87% of the $44.5 bn subsidy bill.

Data check: 16 of 36 reconciliation checks on the source workbook are flagged. Headline deficit figures reconcile; some sub-tables and the historical series do not. See the Data Notes tab before quoting any figure externally.

Data notes and reconciliation
Generated 2026-09-19 15:46 from India_Fiscal_Framework_FY2526_v2.xlsx. Every figure on this portal is rebuilt from the workbook's typed inputs, not from its cached formula results.

What this means: the headline deficit arithmetic (expenditure, receipts, fiscal, revenue and primary deficit, interest) reconciles. The flagged items are inside sub-tables, the financing table and the six-year history. Verify those against Budget at a Glance before quoting them to a client.
Expected = what the other figures in the workbook imply. Workbook = what the workbook's own inputs give.

cells.d: Net financing sources (net dated + T-bills + small savings/GPF + external net) vs fiscal deficit
The workbook labels this total as 'Total Borrowings = Fiscal Deficit' but its sheet-07 formula adds gross and net columns together ($213.9 bn).
Workbook claim: 'fiscal deficit funded 90% by market borrowings' (gross dated G-secs ÷ FD)
Net dated G-secs ÷ FD = 73.6%; net dated + T-bills ÷ FD = 79.3%. 90% is not reproducible on a net basis.
Net receipts ($3.38 bn) exceed gross ($3.30 bn), which is not possible for a net figure.
Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts vs dashboard
Expenditure components (sheet 03) sum $9 mn above the level implied by the dashboard revenue deficit.
Total expenditure typed on FY24-25 RE (Expenditure sheet C28 = 47,161,889) vs Interest/Trends sheets
A stray digit: the FY24-25 RE total is typed as 47,161,889, ten times too large; every other sheet has $491.9 bn. The portal uses $491.9 bn.
Net tax + non-tax (sum of listed items) vs total revenue receipts
Listed revenue items overshoot revenue receipts; one or more revenue lines (likely UT taxes or a non-tax line) is not on the same basis.
FY25-26 BE itemised subsidies vs stated total subsidies
Itemised lines do not add to the stated $44.5 bn; the portal shows the gap as an 'unitemised residual'.
FY24-25 RE itemised subsidies vs stated total subsidies
The workbook's own FY24-25 RE total (formula) reads $21.4 bn because it omits Food; itemised lines sum higher, but still not to the stated figure.
Nominal GDP must rise year on year: FY23-24 → FY24-25 RE
Nominal GDP falls from $3,435.2 bn to $3,403.8 bn. Nominal GDP does not fall in a growth year, so the GDP series (and every ratio built on it) looks misaligned across years.
